resources.string: Current heart rate from the sensor
Look of the app. The home screen widget follows the system theme.
App language. "System" follows the phone language. The voice in headphones speaks the chosen language if the phone has a voice installed for it.
Heart rate is shown in the notification, on the lock screen and in the Now Bar.

The notification stays (Android requires it for background work) but is collapsed: no heart rate, no status bar icon, not on the lock screen and not in the Now Bar. An alert still adds the Mute button.
Bluetooth and notification permissions are required.
Samsung stops background apps. Allow unrestricted battery use, and in Settings -> Battery -> Background usage limits add Pulsar to \"Never sleeping apps\".
The sensor is free: it can be connected on another phone. This phone will not take it back until you press \"Start\".
Looking for the sensor... If it is nearby and worn, recording will start by itself.
Muted until heart rate is back in range
Export CSV of the visible range
Swipe the chart sideways to scroll in time, spread or pinch two fingers to zoom, long press to see a value.

Above the range - 3 long buzzes, below - 4 short ones, repeated every 5 s until heart rate returns or \"Mute\" is pressed. Back in range - 1 short buzz. No data from the sensor for 15 s - long-short-long. Clears with a 3 bpm margin: with an upper limit of 100 it clears at 97.
Heart rate zones (share of max heart rate)
Heart rate zones (max heart rate about %1$d)
Light aerobic: brisk walk, you can talk freely. Builds endurance.
Moderate: talking is hard, breathing is noticeably faster.
Hard: only single words, cannot be sustained for long.

The walk range from age is zone 2; training by default is 70-85%, i.e. zones 3-4. Max is estimated as 220 minus age and may differ by 10-15 beats for a given person, so ranges can be adjusted manually.

Export saves the whole history to one file (CSV in gzip); import adds records from such a file, or from a CSV exported for a period, without duplicates. Imported records are not sent to Health Connect.
New records: %1$d, already present: %2$d, invalid lines skipped: %3$d.
Date of birth sets the walking and training ranges by age; height sets the step length for speed. Month and day of birth are optional.
Each mode has its own range, alert switch and vibration setting. The active mode is chosen on the main screen and is marked on the history charts.
Active now: %1$s. Switch modes on the main screen.
Auto mode needs the step counter: turn on speed by steps in settings.

Auto mode on the main screen picks the mode by itself. Rest - standing still with heart rate in the rest range. Walk - steps without running. Training - heart rate in the training range or running pace, with or without movement. The switch is announced in headphones and by two vibration pulses (per the new mode\'s vibration setting). A change must hold for 1-3 minutes, and after a switch the mode stays for at least 3 minutes. While standing with heart rate between ranges (e.g. recovering after a walk), the mode does not change. In auto mode the alert fires only beyond the overall limits - below rest and above training - and when heart rate stays above the rest range without movement for 2 minutes. Tapping a mode turns auto mode off, and its range is then enforced strictly.
Set your date of birth to use auto.
During these hours and while Do Not Disturb is on, alerts do not vibrate. Voice in headphones stays on.
Approximate speed from the step counter: step rate x step length from your height. Good for walking and running; does not work on a bike or in a vehicle. The step counter uses almost no battery.
More accurate than the step counter and works on a bike, but uses noticeably more battery. Only in this mode.

Speaks only when headphones are connected: \"Heart rate 105, high\", \"Heart rate 96, back in range\", \"Sensor lost\" - and the current heart rate and speed periodically. Music is ducked while speaking.
Shake the phone to hear heart rate
Shake the phone a few times sharply and the voice says the current heart rate and speed. Works only with headphones.
No voice installed for the app language - announcements are in English.
No voice installed for the app language or for English - the voice stays silent.
Search for a lost sensor: %1$d min
For this long after the link is lost the phone actively looks for the sensor and does not fall asleep. After that it waits economically: the sensor reconnects when it shows up, but more slowly.
Health Connect is not available on this phone.
Heart rate is written to Health Connect every 5 minutes.
Write heart rate to Health Connect so Samsung Health and other apps can see it.
No new data: everything is already sent.
Now Bar on the lock screen
Live Updates are off for this app. Turn them on to see heart rate in the Now Bar.
Battery restrictions are not removed: Samsung may stop recording.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and reopen this screen.
Put the sensor on and moisten the contacts: without skin contact it is not visible.
